title: Riemann hypothesis

original_target.title: Riemann hypothesis
original_target.statement: Every nontrivial zero of the analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half.
proof_obligations: Prove the statement for every nontrivial zero, including unbounded heights.
Justify all analytic continuations, limits and equivalences.
A finite zero computation is insufficient.
original_target.research_focus: Reviewed result in docs/RH-RECIPROCAL-COEFFICIENTS.md: for f_n(q)={q/n}, e(q)=1-sum(c_n*f_n(q)) and epsilon^2=sum_{q>=1}|e(q)|^2/(q(q+1)), the identity c_n+mu(n)=sum_{d|n}mu(n/d)*(e(d)-e(d-1)) implies sum_{n=2}^m|c_n+mu(n)|<=3*epsilon*m^(3/2). Hence mass and support size are at least 1/(3000*epsilon^2) for epsilon<=1/100. Seek a sharper aggregate bound or a justified approximation estimate, with an explicit finite statement and all tail terms. Coefficientwise convergence alone gives no norm convergence.
